hints: Identify the normal distribution parameters: travel time $X \sim \mathrm{N}(140, 12^2)$ where $\mu = 140$ and $\sigma = 12$.
Use the symmetry of the standard normal curve to convert the negative $z$-value: $\mathrm{P}(Z < -z) = 1 - \Phi(z)$.
Look up $\Phi(0.667)$ in the standard normal tables and evaluate $1 - \Phi(0.667)$.
walkthrough:
Express the lower-tail probability using the symmetry of the standard normal distribution:
$$\mathrm{P}(X < 132) = \mathrm{P}(Z < -0.667) = 1 - \Phi(0.667)$$

Look up $\Phi(0.667)$ in the standard normal tables:
$$\Phi(0.667) = 0.7477$$
$$\mathrm{P}(X < 132) = 1 - 0.7477 = 0.2523 \approx 0.252$$
teacher_walkthrough: Let $X$ represent the time taken in minutes. We are given $X \sim \mathrm{N}(140, 12^2)$, with mean $\mu = 140$ and standard deviation $\sigma = 12$.

Step 1: Write down the standardisation formula:
$$Z = \frac{X - \mu}{\sigma}$$
Substitute $X = 132$, $\mu = 140$, and $\sigma = 12$:
$$Z = \frac{132 - 140}{12} = \frac{-8}{12} = -\frac{2}{3} \approx -0.6667$$

Step 2: Relate the negative $z$-value to standard normal cumulative table values using symmetry:
$$\mathrm{P}(Z < -0.667) = 1 - \Phi(0.667)$$

Step 3: Read $\Phi(0.667)$ from the Cambridge normal distribution table:
$$\Phi(0.66) = 0.7454$$
$$\text{Add for 7} = 0.0023$$
$$\Phi(0.667) = 0.7454 + 0.0023 = 0.7477$$

Step 4: Subtract from 1 to obtain the tail probability:
$$\mathrm{P}(X < 132) = 1 - 0.7477 = 0.2523 \approx 0.252$$

hints: We are given $\mathrm{P}(X > k) = 0.675$. Since $0.675 > 0.5$, $k$ must be below the mean $\mu = 140$, which means its standardised value $z$ is negative.
By symmetry of the normal curve, an upper tail of $0.675$ corresponds to $\Phi(-z) = 0.675$.
Look up $0.675$ in the main body of the normal distribution table to find the critical value $z_0 = 0.454$, so $z = -0.454$.
walkthrough:
Set up the standardized upper-tail probability:
$$\mathrm{P}(X > k) = 0.675 \implies \mathrm{P}\left(Z > \frac{k - 140}{12}\right) = 0.675$$

Because the area exceeds 0.5, the cutoff lies in the left tail. By symmetry:
$$\Phi\left(-\frac{k - 140}{12}\right) = 0.675$$

Look up the probability 0.675 in the standard normal distribution table:
$$\Phi(0.454) = 0.6751 \implies z = -0.454$$

Equate the standardisation expression to $-0.454$ and solve for $k$:
$$\frac{k - 140}{12} = -0.454$$
$$k - 140 = -0.454 \times 12 = -5.448$$
$$k = 140 - 5.448 = 134.552 \approx 135 \text{ (or } 134.6\text{)}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
We are told that the probability of the travel time taking more than $k$ minutes is 0.675:
$$\mathrm{P}(X > k) = 0.675$$
Because more than $50\%$ of the distribution is greater than $k$, $k$ must lie to the left of the mean 140. Therefore, the standardized value $Z$ is negative.

Step 1: Write down the standardisation formula:
$$Z = \frac{k - \mu}{\sigma} = \frac{k - 140}{12}$$

Step 2: Use symmetry of the normal distribution to locate the $z$-value in the tables:
$$\mathrm{P}(Z > z) = 0.675 \iff \mathrm{P}(Z < -z) = 0.675$$
$$\Phi(-z) = 0.675$$

Step 3: Look up 0.675 in the body of the Cambridge normal table:
$$\Phi(0.45) = 0.6736$$
To reach 0.6750, we need an additional 0.0014:
$$\text{In the differences column, 4 gives } 14$$
Thus:
$$-z = 0.454 \implies z = -0.454$$

Step 4: Solve for $k$:
$$\frac{k - 140}{12} = -0.454$$
Multiply both sides by 12:
$$k - 140 = -0.454 \times 12 = -5.448$$
Add 140 to both sides:
$$k = 140 - 5.448 = 134.552$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $k = 135$ (or 134.6).
